land.text: Kazan and the Middle Volga, the former Volga Bulgaria, 'separating it from the Golden Horde'

predecessors.note: K3: Ulugh Muhammad 'captured Kazan, separating it from the Golden Horde' in 1438; K1: he 'usurped the throne of Kazan with some help from local nobility in 1437 or 1438' and 'the transfer of power from the local Bolgar dynasty to Muhammad was finalized by his son Maxmud in 1445'. The golden-horde dossier (ia-02-a) carries the matching 1438 loss.

land.text: Kazan and its lands, stormed by Ivan IV's army on 2 October 1552; the right bank of the Volga had passed in 1551

successors.note: Resistance continued at Calim and Misatamaq to 1556 (Siege of Kazan page); in 1556 the Russians went down the Volga and conquered Astrakhan.

capitals.name: Kazan
capitals.note: Infobox capital Kazan throughout; the citadel fell on 2 October 1552.

correction.text: the 1440 shape plus Chuvashia, for 1438-1439: the khanate round Kazan taken from the Golden Horde

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1438-1439: Cliopatria starts the Kazan shape in 1440; Ulugh Muhammad 'captured Kazan, separating it from the Golden Horde' in 1438 (infobox elevation 1438). The 1440 shape is taken back two years (with the Chuvashia addition).

correction.text: the 1440 shape plus the whole of Chuvashia (the 'Mountain side' ceded in 1551)

keyframe_review.note: 170,731 km2 (634 cells): Tatarstan (0.92), Ulyanovsk, Mari El (0.6), Chuvashia (0.43), part of Samara, Udmurtia and Kirov. The page gives no area; it says the khanate covered 'contemporary Tatarstan, Mari El, Chuvashia, Mordovia, and parts of Udmurtia and Bashkortostan', with the Volga, Kama and Vyatka as main rivers. Chuvashia is added whole. Mordovia, Udmurtia and Bashkortostan are 'parts' the page does not outline, and Ulyanovsk and Samara (in the shape) are not named: unverified, kept. Valid 1440-1449.

Same extent as 1440 (633 cells), with Chuvashia added. The Moscow-Kazan wars of 1467-1469 moved no frontier on the page: 'Ibrahim overran Vyatka' in 1468 and the 1469 treaty recognised Ibrahim; Vyatka is not shown as Kazan land after it. Valid 1450-1491.
Same extent (631 cells). Ivan III's capture of Kazan on 9 June 1487 made it a Moscow protectorate with Muhammad Amin as khan (Khanate page); the land stays in the Kazan shape. Valid 1492-1501.
639 cells (172,519 km2): the Mordovian edge (0.11) enters the shape. The revolt of 1505 ('Saint John's Day') and the war of 1506 changed no frontier on the page. Valid 1502-1546.

Valid 1547-1550. In 1551 'the lands to the west of the Volga River (Taw yagi) were ceded to Russia' and 'the right bank' went to Russia after the 1551 peace (Siege of Kazan page); Sviyazhsk was built that year.

correction.text: the 1547 shape without Chuvashia (the right bank of the Volga ceded in 1551)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1551-1552: the right bank is Russian after the 1551 peace; the khanate is the left-bank Tatarstan, Mari and Udmurt lands round Kazan until the storming on 2 October 1552. Chuvashia is my reading of the right-bank Mountain side; the page names no towns.

ledger.note: 1438: Ulugh Muhammad takes Kazan from the Golden Horde. 'captured Kazan, separating it from the Golden Horde'; the infobox gives the elevation in 1438 and K1 'usurped the throne of Kazan with some help from local nobility in 1437 or 1438'.

1444-1445: Ulugh Muhammad occupies Nizhny Novgorod. 'in 1444-45 Ulugh Muhammad occupied Nizhny Novgorod and marched on Murom' (K2: 'Ulugh took Nizhny Novgorod' in 1445). A raid-and-hold of a Muscovite town, not an annexation.

1445: the Tatars leave Nizhny Novgorod. Page silent on the withdrawal: after the Battle of Suzdal (7 July 1445, Vasili II captured and ransomed over four months) Ulugh Muhammad 'died a few months later'.
1468: Ibrahim overruns Vyatka. 'Ibrahim overran Vyatka' in answer to the Russian raid on 'Kazan's Vyatka region' (the 1467-1469 succession war in which Ivan III failed to install Qasim).

Autumn 1469: Kholmsky besieges Kazan and the treaty recognises Ibrahim. 'In autumn 1469, Daniil Kholmsky besieged Kazan, and the 1469 treaty recognized Ibrahim.' The page does not say who held Vyatka after.

9 June 1487: Moscow takes Kazan. 'Prince Kholmsky ... laid siege to Kazan on 18 May 1487. The city fell to the Muscovites on 9 June.' Moxammat Amin is proclaimed khan and Kazan becomes a Moscow protectorate (Khanate page: 'In July 1487, Grand Duke Ivan III of Moscow occupied Kazan and seated a puppet leader'). The occupier is Moscow; the end is the protectorate, recorded in the Moscow dossier.

July 1487: the occupation turns into a protectorate (Khanate page: 'In July 1487 ... Ivan III of Moscow occupied Kazan and seated a puppet leader'; month 7 only orders the pair). Page silent on the Muscovite withdrawal; Muhammad Amin rules under Moscow's protection from 1487 (revolts 1496, 1500 and 1505 had 'negligible results'; K1). The protectorate (vassal_start 1487) belongs to the Moscow dossier.

1495-1496: Mamuk of Sibir is briefly khan of Kazan. 'Ibak's younger brother Mamuk was briefly Khan of Kazan' in 1495-96 (Ibak Khan page; the Sibir page: Makhmet 'was briefly Khan of Kazan in 1496'); the Kazan page names Moscow's puppet only. Same state, regime flip (rule 2).

1505: Kazan revolts against Moscow. 'Kazan's rebellion began on Saint John's Day' with Russian merchants massacred at the Kazan Fair; the Tatar-Nogai army advanced on Nizhny Novgorod and Moxammat Amin sued for peace after Arsk Field (22 and 25 June 1506). K1 gives 1496, 1500, 1505 as pro-Ottoman/Crimean revolts and 1521 as the year Kazan 'emerged from the dominance of Moscow'; the end of the protectorate is recorded in the Moscow dossier.

1521: Kazan leaves Moscow's dominance. 'In 1521, Kazan emerged from the dominance of Moscow, concluding a mutual aid treaty with Astrakhan, Crimea, and the Nogai Horde'; another massacre of Russian merchants followed and Vasily III banned trade at the Kazan Fair (K2). The page does not name the Crimean khan (Sahib Giray in other accounts).

1545: Safa Giray is deposed. 'some of these noblemen provoked a revolt in 1545. The result was the deposition of Safa Giray' and Sahgali (Shah Ali), a Moscow ally, took the throne; Safa Giray returned and died in 1549, when his 3-year-old son Utemisgaray was recognised.

region.text: the lands west of the Volga (Taw yagi), the right bank

ledger.note: 1551: the right bank of the Volga passes to Russia. 'At the same time the lands to the west of the Volga River (Taw yagi) were ceded to Russia'; the Siege of Kazan page: 'after peace gave the right bank to Russia', Sviyazhsk was built in 1551. Sahgali was invited a second time at the beginning of 1551 and Utemisgaray sent to Moscow; the 'Mountain side' towns are not named on the pages, Chuvashia is my reading.

region.text: the Kazan Khanate left after the 1551 cession

ledger.note: 2 October 1552: Kazan is stormed. 'Sappers breached the wall ... and Russian soldiers entered the city'; Khan Yadegar Mokhammad (March-October 1552) and the Nogai leader Zaynash were captured. K1 gives 3 October for the entry of the Russians, K2 and K4 2 October. The Volga region was then held by Russia; the rebel governments at Calim and Misatamaq fought on to 1556 (Kazan rebellion).

wars.name: Muscovite-Tatar war of Ulugh Muhammad
wars.outcome: Ulugh Muhammad beats the Muscovites at Belyov (1437), raids Moscow and Kolomna (1439), occupies Nizhny Novgorod in 1444-45 and captures Vasili II at Suzdal on 7 July 1445; the grand duke is ransomed.
wars.note: The Ulugh Muhammad page dates his loss of the Golden Horde to 1436 and the capture of Kazan to 1438.

wars.name: Kazan succession war and Vyatka (1467-1469)
wars.outcome: Ivan III fails to install Qasim; Ibrahim overruns Vyatka in 1468; Kholmsky besieges Kazan in autumn 1469 and the treaty recognises Ibrahim.
wars.note: Ibrahim devastated the Vyatka region again in 1478.

wars.name: Moscow's capture of Kazan (1487)
wars.outcome: Kholmsky besieges Kazan from 18 May and takes it on 9 June 1487; Moxammat Amin is proclaimed khan and Kazan becomes a Moscow protectorate.

wars.name: Kazan revolt and war of 1505-1506
wars.outcome: Russian merchants are massacred at the Kazan Fair; a Tatar-Nogai army advances on Nizhny Novgorod; the Russians are beaten at Arsk Field (22 and 25 June 1506) and Moxammat Amin sues for peace; no frontier moves.

wars.name: Muscovite campaigns against Kazan (1521-1550)
wars.outcome: Belsky besieges Kazan in 1524 and accepts Tatar terms; he burns the city in July 1530 and installs Canghali (murdered 1535); about forty attacks follow in the 1530s-1540s; Safa Giray is deposed in 1545; the expeditions of 1547-48 and 1549-50 achieve little.
wars.note: Safa Giray's December 1540 invasion of Muscovy stalled near Murom.

wars.name: Siege of Kazan (1552)
wars.outcome: Peace gives Russia the right bank in 1551; Sviyazhsk is built; the siege opens at the end of August 1552 and Kazan is stormed on 2 October; the khan Yadegar Mokhammad is captured; resistance lasts to 1556.
wars.note: The page's text starts the siege on 22 August (Old Style), its infobox on 2 September: the sources conflict.

certainty.note: A forest-steppe khanate whose pages name peoples and rivers (the Volga, Kama and Vyatka) but no frontier lines; Cliopatria's shape is an approximate outline. The Volga is the firmest edge after the 1551 cession of the right bank.

sources.title: Khanate of Kazan
sources.note: Infobox (1438-1552), extent, protectorate episodes 1487-1521, 1545 and 1551, the 1551 cession of the right bank, the fall on 3 October.

sources.title: Russo-Kazan Wars
sources.note: Belyov 1437, Suzdal 1445, the 1467-1469 war and Vyatka, 1487, 1505-1506, 1521-1552 campaigns, 2 October 1552.

sources.title: Ulugh Muhammad

sources.title: Ibak Khan
sources.note: Used only for Mamuk's brief khanate in Kazan, 1495-96 (opened for the khanate-of-sibir dossier).

notes:
Cliopatria row: 'Khanate of Kazan' 1440-1551, five shapes of 633-639 cells that differ by a handful of cells (Mordovian edge from 1502): the shape is static. The page dates the khanate 1438-1552; I start at the capture of Kazan in 1438 and end at the storming on 2 October 1552 (Cliopatria's last year is 1551), with new keyframes 1438-1439 and 1551-1552.

Extent: the page lists 'contemporary Tatarstan, Mari El, Chuvashia, Mordovia, and parts of Udmurtia and Bashkortostan' but no area; Cliopatria's shape covers Tatarstan and Mari El well, Chuvashia 43 percent, and adds Ulyanovsk and part of Samara that the page does not name. I add Chuvashia whole (the right bank ceded in 1551) and leave the rest unverified (page budget: 5 pages, one borrowed from the Sibir batch).

Moscow's suzerainty: Moscow took Kazan on 9 June 1487 and made it a protectorate (Muhammad Amin); revolts in 1496, 1500 and 1505 (Kazan page), independence 1505/1521 (pages disagree), a second Muscovite phase under Canghali (Jan Ali, 1532-1535, K2 'placed on the throne' 1530) and Shah Ali (1545, 1551-52). The ledger has no vassal event for Kazan as Moscow's vassal: the schema's vassal events belong to the suzerain, so grand-principality-of-moscow / tsardom-of-russia (group eu-16) should carry vassal_start 1487, vassal_end 1505 or 1521, and the 1531-1535, 1545-1546 and 1551-1552 episodes with counterpart khanate-of-kazan. My occupation_start/end of 1487 is the capture itself (roles reversed: Moscow occupies Kazan's land).

Rebel state: the Kazan rebellion of 1552-1556 (governments at Calim and Misatamaq, Nogai khan Ali Akram; Siege of Kazan page) held land for four years after the khanate ended; it would be a rebel-type dossier (counterpart_needing_dossier), outside this batch's page budget.

Qasim Khanate: founded by Qasim in 1452 in Russian service (Ulugh Muhammad page), on Moscow's land, not Kazan's; no ledger event here. Astrakhan 1556 is not Kazan's.

Disagreements: the Khanate page puts the Russian entry on 3 October, Russo-Kazan Wars and the Siege page on 2 October; the Siege page's text starts the siege 22 August (Old Style) and its infobox 2 September; Khanate page 'July 1487' versus Russo-Kazan Wars 'fell 9 June 1487'; Mamuk of Sibir in 1496 is on the Ibak and Sibir pages, not on the Kazan pages.

Rulers: the Kazan page names khans (19 changes in 115 years, fifteen khans) but gives reign years for only Ulugh Muhammad (1438-1445) and Yadegar Mokhammad (March-October 1552), so no ruler strip is written.
